tools.name: list_calendars
tools.description: List calendars in the org. Org-level API keys see every calendar (agent-owned and shared); agent-scoped keys see only their own agent's calendars. Use this to discover calendar IDs before creating or listing events.

agent_id.description: Filter to calendars owned by this agent. Org keys only — agent-scoped keys are always limited to their own agent and ignore this.

include.description: Pass "all" to include calendars across all agents (org keys only)

tools.name: get_calendar
tools.description: Fetch a single calendar by ID, including its name, timezone, agent status, and default reminders. Agent-scoped keys may only read calendars owned by their agent.

tools.name: create_calendar
tools.description: Create a calendar to hold events and track availability. Calendars are required before creating events — call this first when setting up a new agent. An agent can have multiple calendars (e.g. "Work", "Personal"). Org-level calendars (no agent_id) can be used as shared resources like meeting rooms.

agent_id.description: Agent ID to own this calendar (omit for org-level)

default_reminders.description: Default reminder offsets in minutes before start, inherited by events on this calendar that don't set their own. Omit or null to use the system default (10 min); [] for no reminders.

tools.name: update_calendar
tools.description: Update a calendar's name, timezone, agent status, default reminders, or metadata. Agent-scoped keys may only update calendars owned by their agent.

default_reminders.description: Default reminder offsets in minutes; null for system default, [] for none

tools.name: delete_calendar
tools.description: Delete a calendar (soft delete). Its events are no longer returned and it stops contributing to availability. Agent-scoped keys may only delete calendars owned by their agent.

tools.name: create_booking_page
tools.description: Create a public booking page (a hosted scheduling link) for a calendar. Returns a booking_url to send to a human; when they pick a slot, a confirmed event is created on the calendar and an event.created webhook fires with a booking_page_id field. Set availability_constraints to restrict to weekly working hours; existing calendar events always block slots.

calendar_id.description: Calendar a booking resolves to (from create_calendar/list_calendars).

title.description: Meeting title shown on the page.

description.description: Optional description shown to the booker.

window_days.description: How far ahead bookings are allowed (default 14).

min_notice_minutes.description: Minimum lead time before a bookable slot (default 0).

timezone.description: IANA timezone for display + working hours (default UTC).

availability_constraints.description: Weekly working hours, e.g. {"mon":{"start":"09:00","end":"17:00"}}. Omit/null for any time in the window.

active.description: Whether the page accepts bookings (default true).

tools.name: list_booking_pages
tools.description: List booking pages in the org. Agent-scoped keys see only pages on their own agent's calendars.

tools.name: get_booking_page
tools.description: Fetch a single booking page by ID, including its public booking_url and settings.

tools.name: delete_booking_page
tools.description: Delete (deactivate) a booking page. Its hosted URL stops resolving; already-booked events are unaffected.

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: List events on a calendar or across an agent's calendars, including internally created events and externally synced events from iCal subscriptions (e.g. Google Calendar, Outlook). Provide `calendar_id` OR `agent_id`. Narrow with `start_after`/`start_before` (time window), `status`, and `source`.

calendar_id.description: Calendar ID to list events from. Provide this or agent_id.

agent_id.description: Agent ID to list events for across all of the agent's calendars. Provide this or calendar_id.

start_after.description: Only events starting after this ISO 8601 time

start_before.description: Only events starting before this ISO 8601 time

source.description: Filter by source: "internal" (created via the API) or "external_ical" (synced from an iCal subscription)

expand.description: Expand recurring series into individual occurrence instances within the window. Requires both start_after and start_before (max 366 days apart). Instances carry recurringEventId + originalStartTime.

tools.name: get_event
tools.description: Retrieve a single event by ID, including its title, times, status, location, reminders, and metadata. Works for both internally created events and externally synced iCal events. `calendar_id` is optional — if omitted the calendar is resolved from the event. Provide `calendar_id` to fail fast on cross-calendar typos.

calendar_id.description: Calendar ID that owns the event. Optional — if omitted the calendar is resolved from the event.

tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Create a booking, appointment, meeting, hold, or any scheduled event on a calendar. The calendar_id comes from create_calendar or list_events. Once created, this event blocks the agent's availability during that time and appears in availability queries. Use status="hold" with hold_expires_at to tentatively reserve a slot that auto-releases on TTL.

calendar_id.description: Calendar ID to add the event to

all_day.description: Whether this is an all-day event

status.description: Event status. "hold" creates a tentative reservation that auto-expires at hold_expires_at. Defaults to "confirmed".

reminders.description: Reminder offsets in minutes before start_time (e.g. [10, 1440]). Each fires an event.reminder webhook and shows as an alarm in the iCal feed. Omit or null to inherit the calendar default (then the system default of 10 min); [] for no reminders.

hold_expires_at.description: Required when status="hold". ISO 8601 timestamp 30s-15min in the future. Auto-releases the hold when reached.

hold_priority.description: Only valid with status="hold". Higher-priority overlapping holds pre-empt lower-priority ones. Defaults to 0.

recurrence_rule.description: Make this a recurring series (RFC 5545 RRULE subset, no "RRULE:" prefix), e.g. "FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE;COUNT=12". Supports FREQ=DAILY/WEEKLY/MONTHLY/YEARLY, INTERVAL, COUNT (max 730) or UNTIL, BYDAY (weekly list or monthly ordinal like 2TU/-1FR), BYMONTHDAY (1-28 or -1). start_time must match the rule pattern; expansion is UTC-only. Not allowed with status="hold". Free plan: max 5 recurring events, series must end within 90 days.

tools.name: update_event
tools.description: Reschedule or edit an event — change its title, description, start/end times, location, status, reminders, or metadata. Use this to move an appointment to a new time or update its details. Provide only the fields you want to change. Holds cannot be edited via this tool (use confirm_event / release_event). External iCal events are read-only. `calendar_id` is optional — if omitted it is resolved from the event.

calendar_id.description: Calendar ID that owns the event. Optional — if omitted the calendar is resolved from the event.

description.description: New description, or null to clear it

all_day.description: Whether this is an all-day event

reminders.description: Reminder offsets in minutes before start_time. Omit to leave unchanged, null to inherit the calendar default, [] for no reminders.

recurrence_rule.description: Set/change the recurring series rule (RFC 5545 RRULE subset, full-series semantics), or null to make the event a one-off. Changing the rule or start_time resets cancelled occurrences.

tools.name: cancel_event
tools.description: Delete or cancel an event from a calendar. Use this to remove, cancel, or delete any scheduled event or appointment. The event is marked cancelled and excluded from future availability calculations. For a recurring series, pass `occurrence_start` to cancel just that one occurrence (the series continues); omit it to cancel the whole series. `calendar_id` is optional — if omitted the calendar is looked up from the event. Provide `calendar_id` to fail fast on cross-calendar typos.

calendar_id.description: Calendar ID that owns the event. Optional — if omitted the calendar is resolved from the event. Matches the asymmetry with confirm_event / release_event which never required this arg.

occurrence_start.description: For recurring events only: ISO 8601 start of the single occurrence to cancel. The rest of the series is unaffected.

tools.name: confirm_event
tools.description: Promote a held event to a confirmed booking. The event must currently have status="hold" and its hold_expires_at must not have passed. After confirmation, event.started and event.ended lifecycle webhooks fire at the scheduled times.

event_id.description: Event ID of the hold to confirm

tools.name: release_event
tools.description: Manually release a held event before its hold_expires_at. The event must currently have status="hold". Frees the slot for other agents to book.

event_id.description: Event ID of the hold to release

tools.name: create_agent
tools.description: Register your agent (AI assistant, human participant, or resource) with Chronary so it can own calendars, events, and webhooks.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List all agents in your organization

tools.name: get_agent
tools.description: Fetch a single agent by ID. An agent represents an AI assistant, human, or shared resource (e.g. a meeting room). Agent-scoped API keys may only read their own agent.

tools.name: update_agent
tools.description: Update an agent's name, description, metadata, or status (active/paused). Requires an org-level API key — agent-scoped keys cannot mutate agents.

tools.name: delete_agent
tools.description: Decommission an agent. This marks the agent as decommissioned and revokes all of its scoped API keys. Requires an org-level API key — agent-scoped keys cannot delete agents.

tools.name: get_availability
tools.description: Check when a single agent is free across its Chronary calendars and any human calendars authorized for that agent. This tool is fail-closed: always inspect `availability_state` and `warnings` before using slots. Accepts `start`/`end` or the `start_time`/`end_time` aliases.

agent_id.description: Agent ID to check availability for

duration.description: Requested slot length (15m/30m/45m/1h/2h). Preferred over the deprecated slot_duration. Defaults to 30m.

slot_duration.description: Deprecated alias for `duration` — minimum slot length. Prefer `duration`.

tools.name: find_meeting_time
tools.description: Find slots when multiple agents are free across Chronary calendars and any human calendars authorized for each agent. This tool is fail-closed: always inspect `availability_state` and `warnings` before using slots. Accepts `agents`/`start`/`end` or their aliases.

agents.description: Array of agent IDs to find common free time for. All agents must be free during the returned slots. Alias: agent_ids.

duration.description: Requested slot length (15m/30m/45m/1h/2h). Preferred over the deprecated slot_duration. Defaults to 30m.

slot_duration.description: Deprecated alias for `duration` — minimum slot length. Prefer `duration`.

calendars.description: Additional shared calendar IDs to treat as busy

include_busy.description: Include per-agent busy blocks in response

tools.name: create_connection_link
tools.description: Request human setup of Google Calendar or Microsoft Outlook for a Chronary calendar. Give setup_url to a human; the agent never receives OAuth credentials, provider calendar names, or event data. The secret URL is returned only on first creation. If reused=true and setup_url is null, retain the original URL or cancel this link and create a replacement.

calendar_id.description: Chronary calendar whose owning agent will receive authorized availability

capabilities.description: Request opaque availability, plus optional opt-in event publishing permission

publication_policy.description: Desired publishing policy; a human still chooses the destination

tools.name: get_connection_link
tools.description: Poll a human-calendar setup request. Returns provider-neutral status and resulting connection ID when complete, but never replays the bearer setup URL or exposes human calendar data.

tools.name: cancel_connection_link
tools.description: Cancel a pending human-calendar setup request. This invalidates the setup URL and does not disconnect an already completed Google or Microsoft connection.

tools.name: get_calendar_context
tools.description: Get a calendar's temporal context in a single call: the current event (if one is happening now), the next upcoming event, recent past events, a short upcoming window, and the owning agent's status (idle/working/waiting/error). Use this to answer "what is this agent doing right now?" without issuing multiple list_events queries.

tools.name: create_proposal
tools.description: Create a scheduling proposal — send a set of candidate time slots to one or more participant agents so they can accept, decline, or counter-propose. The organizer agent owns the proposal; once every participant responds, the system auto-resolves to the highest-scoring slot (or cancels if all decline). Requires an org-level API key. Pro plan only.

title.description: Short description of what the meeting is about

calendar_id.description: Calendar the resolved event will be created on

weight.description: Preference for this slot, 0–10 (higher = more preferred). Used to rank candidate slots when the proposal is resolved. Defaults to 1.

calendar_id.description: Calendar to create the event on if this slot is chosen. Defaults to the proposal's top-level calendar_id.

tools.name: list_proposals
tools.description: List scheduling proposals for the org. Filter by status (pending|confirmed|expired|cancelled) or organizer_agent_id. Requires an org-level API key.

tools.name: get_proposal
tools.description: Get a scheduling proposal by id, including its slots and per-participant responses. Requires an org-level API key.

tools.name: respond_to_proposal
tools.description: Submit a response (accept / decline / counter) on behalf of one participant agent to an open proposal. An "accept" requires the slot id from the proposal; a "counter" can suggest alternative slots. When all participants have responded the proposal auto-resolves — no separate resolve call needed in the normal flow. Requires an org-level API key. Pro plan only.

weight.description: Preference for this slot, 0–10 (higher = more preferred). Used to rank candidate slots when the proposal is resolved. Defaults to 1.

calendar_id.description: Calendar to create the event on if this slot is chosen. Defaults to the proposal's top-level calendar_id.

tools.name: resolve_proposal
tools.description: Force-resolve an open proposal using responses collected so far. Picks the highest-scoring slot among those accepted by the most participants and creates a confirmed calendar event. If every response was "decline", the proposal is cancelled instead. Use when you want to close out a proposal without waiting for every participant. Requires an org-level API key. Pro plan only.

tools.name: cancel_proposal
tools.description: Cancel an open proposal. Fires a proposal.cancelled webhook with reason="organizer_cancelled". Requires an org-level API key. Pro plan only.

tools.name: set_availability_rules
tools.description: Set or replace the availability rules on a calendar — buffer times before/after events and optional per-day working hours. When these rules are set, every availability query on this calendar automatically applies them (busy-block expansion for buffers, masking outside working hours). Upsert: overwrites any existing rules.

buffer_before_minutes.description: Minutes of buffer before each event (0–120)

buffer_after_minutes.description: Minutes of buffer after each event (0–120)

working_hours.description: Per-day working hours map in the calendar's timezone; omit keys for off-days. Pass null to remove any working-hours constraint.

start.description: Start of the working window, HH:MM 24-hour, in the rules timezone (e.g. "09:00")

end.description: End of the working window, HH:MM 24-hour, after start (e.g. "17:00")

mon.description: A single day's working hours window

start.description: Start of the working window, HH:MM 24-hour, in the rules timezone (e.g. "09:00")

end.description: End of the working window, HH:MM 24-hour, after start (e.g. "17:00")

tue.description: A single day's working hours window

start.description: Start of the working window, HH:MM 24-hour, in the rules timezone (e.g. "09:00")

end.description: End of the working window, HH:MM 24-hour, after start (e.g. "17:00")

wed.description: A single day's working hours window

start.description: Start of the working window, HH:MM 24-hour, in the rules timezone (e.g. "09:00")

end.description: End of the working window, HH:MM 24-hour, after start (e.g. "17:00")

thu.description: A single day's working hours window

start.description: Start of the working window, HH:MM 24-hour, in the rules timezone (e.g. "09:00")

end.description: End of the working window, HH:MM 24-hour, after start (e.g. "17:00")

fri.description: A single day's working hours window

start.description: Start of the working window, HH:MM 24-hour, in the rules timezone (e.g. "09:00")

end.description: End of the working window, HH:MM 24-hour, after start (e.g. "17:00")

sat.description: A single day's working hours window

start.description: Start of the working window, HH:MM 24-hour, in the rules timezone (e.g. "09:00")

end.description: End of the working window, HH:MM 24-hour, after start (e.g. "17:00")

sun.description: A single day's working hours window

timezone.description: IANA timezone used to interpret working_hours (e.g. America/New_York)

tools.name: get_availability_rules
tools.description: Read the buffer times and working-hours rules configured on a calendar. Returns the rules row, or an error if none are set.

tools.name: clear_availability_rules
tools.description: Remove the availability rules from a calendar, reverting to the default (no buffers, no working-hours mask). Returns the deleted row, or an error if none were set.

calendar_id.description: Calendar whose rules should be cleared

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: List the org's webhook subscriptions with their subscribed event types and active state. Signing secrets are never returned. Requires an org-level API key.

tools.name: get_webhook
tools.description: Get a single webhook subscription by id, including its subscribed event types and active state. The signing secret is never returned. Requires an org-level API key.

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.description: Create a webhook subscription so the org receives HTTP POST notifications when events occur (e.g. event.created, proposal.confirmed). The signing secret is returned ONCE in this response — store it to verify the HMAC-SHA256 signature on delivered payloads. Requires an org-level API key.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint that will receive event deliveries

tools.name: update_webhook
tools.description: Update a webhook subscription — change its delivery URL, the set of subscribed event types, or pause/resume it via active. At least one field must be supplied. Requires an org-level API key.

events.description: Replacement set of event types to subscribe to

active.description: Set false to pause deliveries, true to resume

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description: Permanently delete a webhook subscription. This frees its endpoint slot against the per-plan cap. Requires an org-level API key.

tools.name: list_webhook_deliveries
tools.description: List delivery attempts for a webhook subscription, with per-status counts (pending/delivered/failed). Use this to debug failing deliveries. Requires an org-level API key.

webhook_id.description: Webhook subscription whose deliveries to list

status.description: Filter to a single delivery status

include_payload.description: Include the full event payload sent on each delivery

tools.name: list_ical_subscriptions
tools.description: List an agent's external iCal feed subscriptions (e.g. linked Google Calendar / Outlook feeds), including their sync status and last sync time.

agent_id.description: Agent ID whose iCal subscriptions to list

tools.name: get_ical_subscription
tools.description: Get a single external iCal feed subscription by id, including its sync status, last sync time, and last error.

tools.name: subscribe_ical
tools.description: Link an external iCal feed (e.g. a human's Google Calendar) to an agent's calendar so external events appear in availability calculations. The target calendar must be owned by the specified agent — create the calendar with that agent_id first (org-level calendars without an agent_id cannot host external iCal subscriptions; create a dedicated per-agent calendar for sync targets).

agent_id.description: Agent ID that will own this subscription

calendar_id.description: Calendar ID to sync external events into

url.description: HTTPS URL of the iCal feed (.ics) to subscribe to

tools.name: update_ical_subscription
tools.description: Update an external iCal feed subscription — change its label or its feed URL. Changing the URL forces a full re-sync on the next poll.

url.description: New HTTPS URL of the iCal feed (.ics)

tools.name: delete_ical_subscription
tools.description: Delete an external iCal feed subscription. Events previously synced from the feed are no longer refreshed.

tools.name: sync_ical_subscription
tools.description: Trigger an immediate sync of an external iCal feed subscription instead of waiting for the next scheduled poll. Returns once the sync has been queued.

tools.name: create_scoped_key
tools.description: Create an agent-scoped API key (chr_ak_*) that can only act on behalf of a single agent. Use this to self-provision or rotate per-agent credentials. The plaintext key is returned exactly once in the response — store it immediately, it cannot be retrieved later. Requires an org-level API key.

agent_id.description: Agent ID this key is scoped to

tools.name: list_scoped_keys
tools.description: List all live (non-revoked) agent-scoped API keys for this org. Returns key metadata only (id, prefix, agent_id, label, created_at) — never the plaintext secret. Requires an org-level API key.

tools.name: revoke_scoped_key
tools.description: Revoke an agent-scoped API key by ID. Revocation is permanent (cannot be un-revoked); the key stops authenticating within about a minute. Requires an org-level API key.

key_id.description: ID of the scoped key to revoke

tools.name: get_audit_log
tools.description: List audit-log entries for the calling org — mutating operations and auth-lifecycle events, newest first. Results are clamped to the plan's retention window. Requires an org-level API key (chr_sk_*); agent-scoped keys cannot read the org-wide audit log.

from.description: Start of the window (ISO 8601). Silently clamped to the plan retention window if older.

actor_key_prefix.description: Filter by the API key prefix that performed the action

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response

tools.name: accept_terms
tools.description: Re-accept the current Chronary terms of service on behalf of the calling org. Use this when responses carry the Chronary-Terms-Upgrade-Required header — a material ToS bump otherwise leaves MCP-only agents stuck without a console session. Pass the current tos_version (read it from GET /v1/auth/terms/current). Requires an org-level API key (chr_sk_*); agent-scoped keys cannot accept org-wide terms.

tos_version.description: The terms-of-service version to accept; must match the current version

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Get the calling org's current-period usage and plan limits (agents, calendars, events, API calls, webhooks, availability queries, iCal subscriptions, proposals, scoped keys, holds, cross-calendar queries). Requires an org-level API key (chr_sk_*); agent-scoped keys cannot read org-wide usage.
